samples.summary: Fix treats the symptom, not the load-bearing `cwd`: the driver still spawns children with `cwd: agentDir` because `scorerArgs`/`persistArgs`/`renderArgs` build relative module paths (`path.join("eval", step.module)`). Making those absolute via `HERE` would remove the whole class in about the same number of lines and would not need two path-resolution sites plus a comment explaining the hazard. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260813-eval-scoring-lane-todo.md:393) explicitly defers this as a follow-up, so the scope choice is documented and defensible — recording it only as an approach preference, and as a reminder that any future relative value added to a child argv reopens the same failure with no guard to catch it.
samples.evidence: const doRun = run ?? ((args) => nodeRun(args, { cwd: agentDir, env })); with args[0] = path.join("eval", step.module)

samples.summary: Incident narrative is duplicated three times: ~29 lines of inline comment in score-all.mjs (550-577), ~25 lines of the same story in the new test (score-all.test.mjs), and the canonical write-up in docs/tasks/active/20260813-eval-scoring-lane-todo.md:323-406. The repo files docs by validity; the two-line 'why' plus a pointer to the task doc would carry the same weight without three copies that can drift.

The refusal message now embeds both the resolved path and the raw argument (`... does not exist under <abs> (resolved from "store")`), and the new test pins that exact wording (`/resolved from "no-such-store"/`). This is a diagnostics improvement the task doc asks for, but only the corpus refusal got it — the immediately following run-id refusal (line 590) still prints only `root`, so a relative-root failure on a missing run reads with the same ambiguity the change set out to remove. Inconsistent diagnostics within the same guard block.
